abruzzo.zin: Abruzzo is known for its landscapes and natural environment, parks and nature reserves, and characteristic hillside areas rich in vineyards and olive groves.

aconcagua.zin: Soils: clay and sandy to the east; granite and clay to the west.

ajaccio.zin: The vineyards are planted on granitic soil that is particularly suited to wine-growing.

alexander valley.zin: Further acreage was realigned in 1988 from Chalk Hill AVA to accommodate existing vineyards that long labeled their wines as Alexander Valley but existed across the southeastern boundary.

alicante.zin: In 1958, Alicante Bouschet covered 24,168 hectares (mainly across southern France); by 2011, plantings represented less than 4,000 hectares.

aloxe.zin: In 2007, 38.08 hectares (94.1 acres) of the total Aloxe-Corton vineyard surface consisted of Premier Cru vineyards, all of them for red wine only.

alsace.zin: Alsace's geology is quite varied, with many different kinds of soils represented in the vineyards.

anderson valley.zin: The bottom land soils in Anderson Valley are all either derived from old valley filling material, or more recent alluvial deposits.

australia.zin: In 1853, Australia had less than six hundred hectares of grapes, with only a portion used for winemaking.

barbaresco.zin: The soils of the Barbaresco zone are composed primarily of calcareous marl dating from the Tortonian epoch.

barbera.zin: Barbera can adapt to a wide range of vineyard soils but tends to thrive most in less fertile calcareous soils and clay loam.

barolo.zin: The Central Valley to the west includes the communes of Barolo and La Morra with soils higher in clay, manganese and magnesium oxide.

barossa.zin: The many hectares of vineyards are the most distinctive feature of the area, especially when viewed from the Mengler Hill lookout, positioned on the Barossa Range which forms much of the eastern side of the valley.

batard montrachet.zin: In terms of the Côte d'Or hillside, Bâtard-Montrachet is located below Montrachet, with the Route des Grands Crus running between the two vineyards.

beaujolais.zin: The southern half of the region, also known as the Bas Beaujolais, has flatter terrain with richer, sandstone and clay based soils with some limestone patches.

beaune.zin: Côte de Beaune AOC, often confused with Côte de Beaune-Villages AOC, is an AOC for a small number of vineyards high on the slopes above Beaune.

bergerac.zin: Bergerac soil also features excellent drainage as a result of its proximity to the river Dordogne.

bonnes mares.zin: Bonnes Mares is located a little to the north of the Chambolle-Musigny village, and borders the Route des Grands Crus in the east and the Grand Cru vineyard Clos de Tart in the north.

bordeaux.zin: The soil of Bordeaux is composed of gravel, sandy stone, and clay.

brunello.zin: Vineyards in Montalcino are planted in varied soils—including limestone, clay, schist, volcanic soil and a crumbly marl known as galestro—at altitudes ranging from 149 m to 500 m.

bugey.zin: Vineyards of the two Bugey appellations cover around 500 hectares (1,200 acres) spread over 67 communes in the department of Ain.

burgundy.zin: Burgundy is in some ways the most terroir-oriented region in France; immense attention is paid to the area of origin, and in which of the region's 400 types of soil a wine's grapes are grown.

cabardes.zin: The soil composition varies between chalky clay, limestone and rocky foothill terroir.

cadillac.zin: The grape-pickers are ordered to pick only those clusters or part-clusters which are either fully ripe or have heightened sugar content brought about by noble rot.

california.zin: California has over 477,000 acres (193,000 ha) planted under vines mostly located in a stretch of land covering over 700 miles (1,100 km) from Mendocino County to the southwestern tip of Riverside County.

calistoga.zin: Slope aspect and exposure to the sun in the Calistoga region thus is quite distinct from that in any other AVA within the Napa Valley region.

campo de borja.zin: The soils are mainly dark lime-bearing soils, of average rockiness, good drainage, average level of organic matter and rich in nutrients.

central otago.zin: At around 300 metres (980 ft) elevation, Central Otago's vineyards are protected from New Zealand's characteristic maritime climate by high mountains up to 3,700 metres (12,100 ft) high.

chablis.zin: By the 19th century there were nearly 40,000 hectares (98,840 acres) of vines planted in Chablis with vineyards stretching from the town of Chablis to Joigny and Sens along the Yonne.

chalone.zin: The soils of the Chalone area has limestone and decomposed granite soil and significantly differ from soils of surrounding areas.

chambertin.zin: In 2007, 78.24 hectares (193.3 acres) of the total Gevrey-Chambertin vineyard surface consisted of Premier Cru vineyards.

chambertin clos de beze.zin: In 2008, 14.67 hectares (36.3 acres) of vineyard surface was in production for Chambertin AOC, and 508 hectoliter of wine was produced under the Chambertin designation, corresponding to slightly under 68,000 bottles.

charlemagne.zin: In 2008, only 0.28 hectares (0.69 acres) of the En Charlemagne vineyard surface was in production for Charlemagne AOC, producing a total of 7 hectoliters (essentially three barrels worth of wine).

chassagne.zin: Criots-Bâtard-Montrachet, 1.57 hectares (3.9 acres), is located entirely within Chassagne-Montrachet.

chateauneuf.zin: The characteristic terroir of Châteauneuf-du-Pape comes from a layer of stones called Galets roulés ("pebbles").

chevalier montrachet.zin: In terms of the Côte d'Or hillside, Chevalier-Montrachet is located above Montrachet and is located highest of the five "Montrachet" vineyards.

chianti.zin: The vineyard soils of the area are predominantly marl and chalk.

chinon.zin: The vineyards of the Chinon AOC cover the relatively steep banks of the Vienne as well as the less steep slopes running northward from the hills above Chinon to the Loire.

cigales.zin: The soil is light brown in color and is formed by lime-bearing sand and gypsum-bearing clays, lying on a subsoil of clays and marls.

clos de la roche.zin: The largest landholder in Clos de la Roche is Domaine Ponsot, who own 3 of the original 4 hectares of the vineyard, which has since been expanded to the current 13.41 hectares.

clos de tart.zin: Clos de Tart is a monopole, owned in its entirety by the French holding company Groupe Artemis since its 2017 purchase from the Mommessin family.

clos de vougeot.zin: The soils of the middle part of the vineyard consist of softer limestone with clay and some gravel, and moderate drainage.

clos des lambrays.zin: Clos de Lambrays totals 8.84 hectares (21.8 acres) and most of it (8.66 hectares (21.4 acres)) is owned by the winery Domaine des Lambrays.

clos saint denis.zin: Clos Saint-Denis was originally a church-owned vineyard, belonging to the Collégiale de St-Denis de Vergy, named after Saint Denis.

colares.zin: Because grapevines there are grown directly in the sand, and phylloxera aphids cannot live on sand, Colares vineyards are some of the only European vines that are not grafted upon American rootstocks.

colli orientali.zin: The climate and soil is very similar to the neighboring DOC of Collio Goriziano and the two region share many winemaking similarities as well.

columbia valley.zin: The viticultural area includes the drainage basin of the Columbia River and its tributaries through much of Washington.

condrieu.zin: The Condrieu AOC covers more than 500 acres (202 ha) of hilly terrain located along a 12 miles (19 km) stretch of the Rhône.

coombsville.zin: Coombsville lies upon wide alluvial deposits created by the weathering of the hillsides and its soils contain abundant rock, gravel and, in some areas, layered with volcanic ash deposits from Mount George.

coonawarra.zin: Coonawarra's terra rossa soil is one of the notable terroirs of the New World, covering an area of just 15 km x 2 km north of Penola.

corbieres.zin: Due to its size and geography, Corbières encompasses an enormous variety of soil types and microclimates.

corsica.zin: The average elevation of vineyards in Corsica is 300 metres (1,000 ft) above sea levels where they are susceptible to strong winds.

corton.zin: The vineyard surface of these three appellations totalled 147.5 hectares (364 acres) in 2008.

corton charlemagne.zin: In 1998, the combined Corton-Charlemagne and Charlemagne grand cru contained 51 hectares (130 acres) that produced 2325 hectoliters of Grand Cru white wine.

costieres.zin: The soil depth from 3 to 15 metres is largely responsible for the variations of style within this AOC.

cote rotie.zin: The Côte-Rôtie is subdivided into two main sections of varying soil compositions - the Côte Brune ("brown slope") in the north on dark, iron-rich schist and the Côte Blonde with its pale granite and schist soil.

coteaux du layon.zin: The AOC of Bonnezeaux is located in the eastern part of the Coteaux du Layon area, and has about 110 hectares (270 acres) of vineyards.

cotes du rhone.zin: The vines are cultivated on very steep slopes making the harvest extremely arduous.

dry creek.zin: At the turn of the 20th century, Dry Creek Valley was one of California's most prominent producers of Zinfandel with nine wineries and 883 acres (357 ha) of vineyards contributing to the state's wine boom.

dundee.zin: The Yamhill-Carlton region, to the Dundee area's west and northwest, has soils derived from marine sediments and ocean floor volcanic basalt with high water holding capacity.

echezeaux.zin: Échezeaux, which in the early 2000s had 80 vineyard owners, has a reputation for being somewhat variable in quality, which is a reputation it shares with its likewise much sub-divided neighbour Clos de Vougeot.

edna valley.zin: With moderate sunshine, cool maritime fog, and rich oceanic and volcanic soils, the Edna Valley appellation has California's longest growing season.

el dorado.zin: Varying in elevation and topography, each soil offers good drainage and the nutrients needed to encourage vines producing rich, deeply flavored grapes.

faugeres.zin: The appellation area covers 1800 hectares, and consists mainly of primary, schist soils.

fixin.zin: Premiers Crus located within the commune of Fixin: Arvelets, Hervelets, Clos du Chapitre, Clos Napoléon, and Clos de la Perrière.

gaillac.zin: On the Gaillac terroir, the variety Fer Servadou is known as Braucol.

gevrey.zin: In 2007, 78.24 hectares (193.3 acres) of the total Gevrey-Chambertin vineyard surface consisted of Premier Cru vineyards.

gioia del colle.zin: Gioia del Colle's climate is mediterranean (Köppen Csa), but it has peaks of continentality due to the altitude and the distance from the sea.

grands echezeaux.zin: Grands Échezeaux borders on Clos de Vougeot and its wall in the east and north, and on Échezeaux in the west and south.

hermitage.zin: With 345 acres (140 ha) of vines, in soil composed greatly of granite and gravels, Hermitage produces 730,000 bottles of mostly red wines, annually.

howell mountain.zin: The soil in the appellation is volcanic with excellent drainage.

hungary.zin: Hungary lies within the Danube River's drainage basin and is dominated by great lowland plains.

irouleguy.zin: The vineyards are often located on extremely steep slopes with inclines of up to 60°.

ischia.zin: Vineyards planted within the 179 hectares (440 acres) boundaries of the DOC tend to be on volcanic soils with high pumice, phosphorus and potassium content.

julienas.zin: The area of Juliénas has one of the most varied soil types in the region and includes schist, diorite, sandstone and some clay.

knights valley.zin: Mallocomes Valley would later be renamed "Knights Valley." It's documented that Knight grew 17 acres (6.9 ha) of wine grapes, thought to have been planted in 1874, and shipped to wineries in Napa Valley.

la clape.zin: The Cers blows through this corridor towards the Mediterranean, striking the topography of the Massif de la Clape, sometimes with enough force to uproot large trees on the massif's steep slopes with flat soils.

la grande rue.zin: The grand cru appellation occupies an area of 1.6525 hectares, 1.4207 in the historic lieu-dit Grande Rue, and parcels of .2096h and .0222h in "les Gaudichots".

la mancha.zin: The La Mancha DO, which spans parts of Albacete and Cuenca, is the world's largest wine DO, covering 190,980 hectares (471,900 acres) and 182 municipalities.

lalande de pomerol.zin: The estates of Néac feature clay and gravelly soil more commonly seen in neighboring Pomerol, while the estates of Lalande lie on sandier soil.

languedoc.zin: The composition of soil in the Languedoc varies from the chalk, limestone and gravel based soils inland to more alluvial soils near the coast.

lirac.zin: The terroir in Lirac is somewhat similar to Châteauneuf-du-Pape both in variety and hours of sun (2700).

loire.zin: The soil around the Touraine area is a variety of limestone with excellent drainage that is known as tuffeau which is the same material used to build many of the famous Loire Valley Châteaux.

macon.zin: Mâcon is surrounded by a vineyard of 12,355 acres (5,000 ha) which produces 49 million bottles of wine including the famous crus like Saint-Véran or Pouilly-Fuissé.

malleco.zin: The volcanic soil in Malleco, composed mainly of sand and clay, are reasonably well drained.

marcillac.zin: The vines are planted in red clay soils rich in iron oxide that are known locally as rougiers.

margaret river.zin: Margaret River is the major geographical indication wine region in southwest Western Australia, with 5,840 hectares under vine and 215 wineries as at 2012.

margaux.zin: Margaux contains 1,413 hectares (3,490 acres) of vineyards, making it the second largest appellation in the Haut-Médoc (after Saint-Estèphe).

marsannay.zin: In 2008, 227 hectares (560 acres) of vineyard surface was in production for Marsannay wine, of which 32.01 hectares (79.1 acres) were used for Marsannay rosé.

mcminnville.zin: According to the petitioner, this higher elevation causes the McMinnville viticultural area to have distinctive soils and climate when compared to the lower parts of the Willamette Valley.

menetou salon.zin: Menetou-Salon is the name of an Appellation d'origine contrôlée for wine (AOC), with vineyards extending over 330 hectares (820 acres) over the hill.

meursault.zin: In 2007, 96.97 hectares (239.6 acres) of the total Meursault vineyard surface consisted of Premier Cru vineyards, of which 0.82 hectares (2.0 acres) red Meursault Premier Cru.

monbazillac.zin: Only wine made from grapes grown in Monbazillac that are affected by the "noble rot" (Botrytis cinerea) can be sold under the Monbazillac designation.

montalcino.zin: The lower slopes of the Montalcino hill itself are dominated by vines and olive orchards.

monthelie.zin: In 2007, 35.57 hectares (87.9 acres) of the total Monthélie vineyard surface consisted of Premier Cru vineyards, of which 33.94 hectares (83.9 acres) red and 1.63 hectares (4.0 acres) white Monthélie Premier Cru.

montrachet.zin: Montrachet and Bâtard-Montrachet cross the communal border and are shared with Chassagne-Montrachet, totaling respectively 7.99 hectares (19.7 acres) and 11.24 hectares (27.8 acres) of vineyards in 2008.

moon mountain.zin: Moon Mountain's volcanic origins gave the area's winemakers cause to petition for a separate AVA title, which was approved in 2013.

moriles.zin: The white soil of Montilla-Moriles is rich in calcium carbonate; the soil and subsoil are formed by soft loams, poor in natural organic material, and are not very fertile.

mosel.zin: In southeastern Luxembourg, along the country's 42 km river border with Germany, 1 290 hectares of vines are used to produce wine under the designation Appellation Contrôlée Moselle Luxembourgeoise.

mount veeder.zin: The soils have developed from sandstones and shales which are absent on the southwest slopes of the Mayacamas Mountains in Sonoma County.

muscadet.zin: The soil in this area is rich in magnesium and potassium, made up of clay, gravel and sand above subsoils of gneiss, schist, granite and volcanic rock.

musigny.zin: In 2008, 10.32 hectares (25.5 acres) of vineyard surface was in production within the Musigny AOC, and 307 hectoliter of wine was produced, of which 284 hectoliter red wine and 23 hectoliter white wine.

nero d avola.zin: In 2020, Sonoma County's Hanna Winery planted 2.4 acres of Nero on a Hillside block in their Alexander Valley Vineyard.

new zealand.zin: The vineyards are the highest in New Zealand – at 200 to 400 metres (660 to 1,310 ft) above sea level – on the steep slopes of lakesides and the edges of deep river gorges, often in glacial soils.

oakville.zin: The contribution of small percentages of metamorphic clasts (such as serpentine and chert) on the Rutherford fan soils contributes to minor soil differences between the Rutherford viticultural area and Oakville.

oregon.zin: The Oregon subsection has 5 wineries and 1,200 acres (486 ha) planted.

ornellaia.zin: From a 91 ha (220-acre) estate, the vineyard area extends 76 ha (190 acres) in two separate locations, Ornellaia and Bellaria.

penedes.zin: The Alt Penedès vineyards are at an elevation of up to 800 metres (2,600 ft) above sea level, where the native Parellada is the dominant variety.

pomerol.zin: The soils of the Pomerol region are very diverse with a mixture of gravel, sand and clay scattered across the plateau.

pommard.zin: In 2007, 116.44 hectares (287.7 acres) of the total Pommard vineyard surface consisted of Premier Cru vineyards.

portugal.zin: The quality and great variety of wines in Portugal are due to noble castas, microclimates, soils and proper technology.

pouilly fuisse.zin: West of Mâcon the land rises up to form Mont de Pouilly and other limestone hills, covered in the alkaline clay that best suits Chardonnay.

priorat.zin: The area is characterised by its unique terroir of black slate and quartz soil known as llicorella.

provence.zin: The soil across Provence is varied, lacking uniformity and generalization.

puligny.zin: Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet, 3.53 hectares (8.7 acres), and Chevalier-Montrachet, 7.47 hectares (18.5 acres), are located entirely within Puligny-Montrachet.

quincy.zin: The soil has three layers: a soil made up of sand and gravel on an underlay of clay, a sandy soil covered by red sand and a sandy-silt soil on a clayey-sand or clay with slightly sandy soil.

ribbon ridge.zin: Vineyard activity began on Ribbon Ridge in 1980 with the establishment of Ridgecrest Vineyards by Harry Peterson-Nedry beginning with 12 acres (5 ha).

ribeira sacra.zin: Most of the vineyards in Ribeira Sacra are planted along the Miño, Sil, Cabe and Bibei river canyons, with slopes that can reach nearly 100% gradient in some points.

ribeiro.zin: Most of Ribeiro's soils are granitic, with sandy loam textures.

romanee.zin: In 2008, 153.6 hectares (380 acres) of vineyard surface was in production for Vosne-Romanée wine at village and Premier Cru level, and 5,955 hectoliters of wine was produced, corresponding to almost 800,000 bottles.

romanee conti.zin: In the 1750s, the price of de Croonembourg's La Romanée wine was six to seven times as high as Clos de Vougeot wine, and it was sold in feuillettes, half-size 114 litre barrels.

romanee saint vivant.zin: In 1966, the last member of the Marey-Monge family leased the remaining 5.28 hectares (13.0 acres) to Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, and also gave them an option to be first buyers if the vineyard would come up for sale.

roussillon.zin: Côtes du Roussillon-Villages is a sub-appellation in the northern half of the appellation in the valley of the river Agly, from the best slopes around the valley.

russian river.zin: The predominant soils of the Russian River Valley viticultural area are Huichica Loam, Yolo Clay Loam, and Yolo Silt Loam, as depicted on the Sonoma County Soil Survey map (USDA, 1972), in the petition.

rutherford.zin: Rutherford, the seventh sub-appellation designated within Napa Valley AVA, is known for its unique terroir particularly with its Cabernet Sauvignon.

saint aubin.zin: Another group is situated on an east-facing slope in the side valley, forming a band immediately above the village of Saint-Aubin itself.

saint chinian.zin: To the south of the appellation, beyond the village of Saint-Chinian, the soils are quite clayey and chalky.

saint julien.zin: The tradition of wine-growing in Saint-Julien-Beychevelle and the way in which its terroir has come to prominence parallels the history of the Médoc wines in general.

saint nicolas.zin: The AOC was created by a decree on July 31, 1937, covering about 800 hectares in the commune of Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil in the département of Indre-et-Loire.

saint romain.zin: Most vineyards of Saint-Romain are located on slopes of various directions.

sainte croix du mont.zin: The appellation extends over 500 hectares (1,200 acres) and the grape varieties grown are Sémillon, Sauvignon and Muscadelle.

sancerre.zin: Heading closer to the city of Sancerre the soil picks up more gravel mixed with the limestone and tends to produce more light bodied wines with delicate aroma.

santa barbara.zin: By the late 1800s, there were 45 vineyards in the area including a 150 acres (61 ha) vineyard on Santa Cruz Island.

santa cruz.zin: The appellation encompasses some 480,000 acres (750 sq mi) extending through Santa Cruz, Santa Clara and San Mateo counties.

santa maria.zin: The soils are mainly sand, sandy loam, and loam on the valley floor, but are mixed sandy, clay, shaly, and silt loams on mountain slopes.

santa ynez.zin: The Shedd-Santa Lucia-Diablo association consists of steep, well-drained shaly clay loams and silty clay loams.

santenay.zin: In 2007, 130.02 hectares (321.3 acres) of the total Santenay vineyard surface consisted of Premier Cru vineyards, of which 110.12 hectares (272.1 acres) red and 12.90 hectares (31.9 acres) white Santenay Premier Cru.

santorini.zin: Because of its unique ecology and climate – and especially its volcanic ash soil – Santorini is home to unique and prized produce such as the Santorini cherry tomato.

saussignac.zin: The grapes used are generally Sémillon grapes which have been affected by Botrytis cinerea.

sauternes.zin: Sauternes wine is made from Sémillon, sauvignon blanc, and muscadelle grapes that have been affected by Botrytis cinerea, also known as noble rot.

savennieres.zin: Savennières-Roche-aux-Moines covers 33 hectares (82 acres) and Savennières-Coulée-de-Serrant covers 7 hectares (17 acres).

sherry.zin: The albariza soil is the best for growing the Palomino grape, and by law, 40 percent of the grapes making up a sherry must come from albariza soil.

sicily.zin: Sicily has long been noted for its fertile soil, which is the result of past volcanic eruptions.

sierras de malaga.zin: The soil is mostly alluvial with carbonates present on the surface, although near the coastline the composition is more varied, including clay, quartz and mica.

soave.zin: The classico zone was first delineated by Veneto authorities in 1927 and originally encompassed 2,720 acres (1,100 ha) of hillside vineyards within the Soave zone.

somontano.zin: The vines here enjoy a dark sandy-clay soil, particularly high in lime content and rich in alluvial matter.

sonoma.zin: In 1900, there were approximately 4,000 acres (1,600 ha) of vineyards in the Sonoma Valley producing hundreds of thousands of gallons of premium wine.

south africa.zin: Vineyard soil types range from decomposed granite on the hillside near the mountains to sandy, alluvial loam in the valleys near the rivers.

sta rita.zin: Rita Hills" AVA and the adjacent Santa Ynez Valley AVA show a distinct difference resulting from a high percentage of alluvial and marine sand within the Sta.

stellenbosch.zin: The soils of Stellenbosch range from dark alluvium to clay.

tavel.zin: The 933 hectares produce an average yield of 42 hectolitres per hectare The vineyards are located in the commune of Tavel only.

terra alta.zin: The soils are clayey, with a good lime content, poor in organic material, with a significant proportion of sizable elements which allows for good drainage.

tokaji.zin: The soil is of volcanic origin, with high concentrations of iron and lime.

tulbagh.zin: Accordingly, Tulbagh enjoys some of the most diverse and attractive conditions for viticulture in the Cape, and the differences in terroir available to wine makers allow for a wide diversity of distinctive wines.

utiel requena.zin: The soils are dark in colour with a high lime content, permeable and poor in organic matter.

valencia.zin: The Moscatel sub-zone is located at the western boundary of the city of Valencia and the vineyards rise from sea level to an altitude of 100 m.

verdicchio.zin: In her book, Jancis Robinson's Guide to Wine Grapes, Robinson reports in 1996 that there were nearly 10,000 acres (4,000 ha) of Verdicchio found mostly in the provinces along the Adriatic coast.

volnay.zin: In 2007, 132.68 hectares (327.9 acres) of the total Volnay vineyard surface consisted of Premier Cru vineyards.

vosne.zin: In 2008, 153.6 hectares (380 acres) of vineyard surface was in production for Vosne-Romanée wine at village and Premier Cru level, and 5,955 hectoliters of wine was produced, corresponding to almost 800,000 bottles.

vouvray.zin: Vineyards are usually planted on the plateau above the river bank in soils composed of gravel and clay on top of tuffeau.

wachau.zin: The vineyard soils of the Wachau are varied but consist primarily of rock outcrops with occasional layers of loess.

walla walla.zin: The soils of the Walla Walla Valley consist largely of wind-deposited loess, which provides good drainage for vines.

washington.zin: Most of the vineyards planted on the Washington side of the appellation are located on southward facing slopes along the river where they can receive some protection from the winds.

willamette.zin: The appellation is the wine growing region which encompasses the drainage basin of the Willamette River.

yakima.zin: The appellation encompasses 600,000 acres (938 sq mi) mostly contained within Yakima County, Washington with the eastern edge extending into Benton County.

yamhill.zin: Hyndman, the soils of the Yamhill-Carlton, formed in the Eocene era, are derived from marine sediments and ocean floor volcanic basalt that have a high water-holding capacity with moderate to high erosion levels.

yountville.zin: The Yountville area is unusual as a Napa Valley floor viticultural region in that it is not dominated geomorphically by large alluvial fans.

toelichting: Eén zin per plek over de grond, de helling, het klimaat of de geschiedenis. Geen oordeel en geen jaargang: dit verandert niet per oogst. De zin is machinaal gekozen uit het artikel en machinaal teruggezocht. De app toont hem als citaat met de bron en een link, zoals de licentie vraagt. Zinnen die de plek niet noemen én een andere eigennaam bevatten zijn verwijderd, want die gaan over de buren.
